The shaft is a solid circular bar of diameter d = 30 mm and length L = 1200 mm, made of AISI 1020 steel with shear modulus G = 76 923.1 MPa.
The shaft is clamped (fixed) at x = 0 and free at x = 1200 mm.
The loading is pure torsion with two discrete torques applied along the axis: T₁ = +200 000 N·mm at x = 1200 mm and T₂ = −200 000 N·mm at x = 400 mm.
No transverse shear force, no bending moment, no distributed torque, and no other load acts on the shaft.
Small-deformation, linear-elastic behavior is assumed; the cross-section remains plane and undistorted (Saint-Venant torsion of a prismatic circular bar).
All numerical work uses units of N, mm, and MPa.
Compute the polar moment of inertia J = π d⁴ / 32 for the solid circular cross-section.
State the sign convention for internal torque (right-hand rule about the +x axis) and the governing relation for internal torque in each segment, T(x) = algebraic sum of all externally applied torques on the portion of the shaft to the right of the cut.
Determine the internal torque T in segment 1 (0 ≤ x ≤ 400 mm) and in segment 2 (400 mm ≤ x ≤ 1200 mm).
For each segment, compute the maximum torsional shear stress at the outer surface using τ_max = T·c / J, where c = d/2 = 15 mm.
Compute the angle of twist in each segment using Δθ = T·L_seg / (G·J), then sum the contributions to obtain the total angle of twist θ at x = 1200 mm relative to the fixed end at x = 0.
Report all intermediate values (J, T per segment, τ_max per segment, Δθ per segment) and the final θ in both radians and degrees.
State explicitly that the wall reaction torque is zero (since T₁ + T₂ = 0), and note that segment 1 carries zero internal torque and therefore contributes zero shear stress and zero twist.
